stem: Use an explicitly added local conservative two-joint model at q=(0,0): H=[[3,1],[1,2]] kg·m², D1=∂H/∂q1=[[1,0],[0,0]], D2=∂H/∂q2=[[0,1],[1,2]], in kg·m²/rad. Let v=q̇=(1,2) rad/s, a=q̈=(2,−1) rad/s² and g=∇V=(4,3) N·m. Use physical kinetic energy K=½vᵀHv and the explicitly corrected relation τ=Ha+Ḣv−∇K+g, where Ḣ=D1v1+D2v2. Which combined torque and physical-consistency conclusion is correct?

options.text: τ=(13.75,10) N·m; H is symmetric positive definite at this state, but a low black-box torque-fit error alone does not guarantee that structure.
τ=(13.5,7) N·m; low black-box torque-fit error itself guarantees a symmetric positive-definite implicit inertia matrix at all configurations.
τ=(8.5,−3) N·m; H is symmetric positive definite at this state, but a low black-box torque-fit error alone does not guarantee that structure.
τ=(13.5,7) N·m; H is symmetric positive definite at this state, but a low black-box torque-fit error alone does not guarantee that structure.

assumptions: All numerical coefficients and the local state are added, not measurements or output from the omitted DeLaN2R implementation.

The stated corrected formula uses physical K with one-half. p1764 calls the doubled quadratic T kinetic energy, while p1765 halves a gradient of already physical energy; those source qualifications remain explicit.
D1 and D2 are local derivatives of a smooth symmetric H. The supplied SPD test is local and does not certify H at arbitrary configurations.
